transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-09 16:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM); Avery (CTO Emberlyte), Rohan (Head of ML), Jenna (Dev Lead)

Summary: quick discovery re: Redwood PLG quickstart, customer interested in self-serve hosted API to demo features quickly then evaluate Dedicated/Private for production. Security (KMS, SSO), throughput and cost concerns discussed.

[00:00] Sofia (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intro  i'm sofia from Redwood, this is Ethan our solutions eng and Maya on success. how's everyone?
[00:18] Avery (CTO): good; thanks. we are on a tight timeline  demo to execs in three weeks so need to get something live fast.
[00:30] Sofia: totally. that's exactly where our PLG quickstart usually helps  free credits, quick api keys, and sample apps to get to first token in minutes. what's your current stack for hosting inference?
[00:46] Rohan (Head of ML): we're mostly on GCP, use a mix of open weights via company infra and some hosted endpoints. latency's been variable; for the demo we just need sub-300ms p95 on single-turn queries.
[01:05] Ethan (SE): ok that's helpful. just to clarify when you say single-turn, is that 512 tokens or shorter?
[01:12] Rohan: shorter, like 60-80 tokens. but we do plan to expand later.
[01:18] Jenna (Dev Lead): also curious how quickly our product folks can get a token running  you mentioned time-to-first-token earlier?
[01:25] Sofia: yeah, our quickstart is built for that  sign up, claim free credits, create API key, curl or SDK example. most teams hit first token in 5-15 minutes if they follow the steps.
[01:36] Avery: that's promising. what's the difference between hosted and dedicated in terms of onboarding time?
[01:42] Ethan: hosted is immediate  you get api keys and can call models. dedicated requires a reserved capacity contract and some provisioning on our side, so it takes longer, usually a few days to a week depending on commit and infra. for the demo you almost always want hosted first and then transition to dedicated.
[02:02] Rohan: what about data  we don't want logs leaving our org, need audit logs and KMS.
[02:09] Maya (CSM): we can toggle retention and there are enterprise controls; for private we support customer KMS/HSM and VPC options. SSO/SAML and RBAC are available for SRE and dev teams.
[02:26] Avery: okay perfect. any SOC/ISO certifications we should know about?
[02:30] Sofia: we have SOC 2 in progress / SOC 2 type II targeted for Q4, and we have ISO 27001 in roadmap. I will attach our security overview doc; Ethan can add specifics about encryption at rest and audit logging.
[02:45] Ethan: yep  also to note there are options to route requests regionally to satisfy data residency if needed.
[02:52] Jenna: for the quickstart, are there client SDKs in python/js?
[02:56] Sofia: yeah python and node. we also have curl examples and a sample react app you can fork.
[03:03] Rohan: ok on pricing  do you charge per token for hosted? and how does dedicated pricing work?
[03:10] Sofia: hosted is usage-based per token and per-embedding units; dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits and predictable throughput. i can send an example pricing spreadsheet.
[03:20] Avery: we might do hosted for demo to minimize friction and then evaluate dedicated for internal rollout.
[03:25] Ethan: sounds common. for the benchmark run we usually propose a small PoC  we run 1k requests across typical prompt shapes, measure latency and cost, and suggest batching/caching config.
[03:40] Rohan: that would be useful. how hard is it to test model variants?
[03:44] Ethan: easy via the model catalog in the API  you can change model param on the request. We have pre-curated models and variants and can suggest quantized options for lower cost.
[03:55] Jenna: any known gotchas for integrating with our GCP infra?
[03:59] Ethan: not really, calls are standard REST and SDKs; if you need tight VPC egress rules we can provide private deployment info.
[04:10] Sofia: quick note on pitfalls  sometimes teams confuse KV cache with caching  our KV cache is for autoregressive generation speedups, while prefix caching is for repeated prompts. rookie mistake but easy to avoid.
[04:28] Rohan: haha yes we've seen weird throughput drops when cache isn't warmed.
[04:33] Avery: can you share an example of time-to-first-token from customers?
[04:37] Sofia: we have an internal stat  median time-to-first-token for PLG flows is about 8 minutes; with our quickstart sample app it's usually <10. i'll include a step-by-step guide.
[04:50] Ethan: for the demo we'll also recommend a model choice that balances latency and quality. sometimes folks start with a lighter quantized model for snappy UX.
[05:00] Jenna: for authentication we want SSO and rotating keys  can we rotate keys programmatically?
[05:05] Maya: yes, API keys can be rotated and we support SSO provisioning via SAML/Okta; RBAC for team roles is supported.
[05:15] Rohan: one more on security  can logs be disabled for hosted? we don't want prompts stored in plain text.
[05:22] Ethan: hosted has configurable retention policies; for strict requirements we usually recommend Dedicated or Private with customer-managed KMS where you control logs.
[05:33] Sofia: i'll note that in the follow-up.
[05:36] Avery: what's the typical timeline for a small benchmark and then a pilot?
[05:40] Ethan: benchmark can run in 1-2 weeks depending on dataset prep; pilot with dedicated capacity is usually 4-8 weeks for procurement and provisioning.
[05:52] Rohan: procurement can move fast if we show clear cost savings vs current infra. do you have a model for cost comparisons?
[06:00] Sofia: yes we have a cost/per-token breakdown and a quantization recommendations guide; Ethan will tailor it to your workloads.
[06:08] Jenna: for the demo we also want some canned prompt sets for QA.
[06:12] Ethan: we'll share sample prompt sets and an eval harness. we can also run a quick quality check vs a baseline model.
[06:22] Avery: any required cooperation from our side to get free credits and quickstart running?
[06:26] Sofia: just sign up, verify email and accept TOS; i'll send a guide with the exact steps and the free credits link. you can be calling the API in minutes.
[06:35] Rohan: great. what about rate limits for the free credits tier?
[06:39] Sofia: there are conservative rate limits to prevent abuse; if you need higher throughput for the benchmark we can temporarily increase limits for the PoC.
[06:48] Jenna: ok that addresses most of our demo concerns.
[06:51] Avery: can we do a brief run-through of the quickstart flow now?
[06:55] Sofia: sure  i'll share my screen and show the sign-up but since this is recorded i'll just summarize: sign up -> verify -> create API key -> run curl POST to /v1/generate with model param -> get tokens back. SDKs have helper functions.
[07:15] Rohan: sounds straightforward.
[07:18] Ethan: for the benchmark we'll ask for a representative set of prompts and expected p95 targets. if you can share the dataset we can run a small suite.
[07:28] Avery: i'll have Jenna pull together the dataset by monday.
[07:32] Jenna: yes we'll do that.
[07:35] Sofia: next steps recap  i'll email the quickstart doc, free credits link, pricing sheet; Ethan will prepare benchmark plan and sample payloads; you share dataset and latency targets.
[07:48] Rohan: timeline looks good. any other questions?
[07:52] Avery: one more  continuity: once we move from hosted to dedicated, what's the migration path?
[07:58] Ethan: we provide pinned model versions, routing policies, and we can do canary rollouts. stateful caches are different across deployments but we migrate keys and provide compatibility layers.
[08:13] Sofia: ok i think we're aligned. i'll send follow-up and we'll lock a demo + benchmark slot for next week. thanks everyone.
[08:23] Meeting end.
